name: MLX90614 infrared thermometer
description: Melexis non-contact infrared thermometer: object temperature -70 to 380 °C and sensor temperature -40 to 125 °C at 0.02 °C resolution (±0.5 °C around room temperature), read over SMBus/I2C at up to 100 kHz, default address 0x5A. Sold as: GY-906 MLX90614 infrared thermometer module (MLX90614ESF-BAA, 4-pin: VIN, GND, SCL, SDA, with 662K 3.3 V regulator and pull-ups), runs on 3.3–5 V.
eli5: Points at something and tells you how hot it is without touching it.

pins.name: VIN
pins.description: Supply 3.3–5 V (on-board 3.3 V regulator feeds the 3 V MLX90614BAA)

pins.name: SDA
pins.description: SMBus/I2C data (PWM output if reprogrammed; pull-up on board)

supplierQuery: GY-906 MLX90614 infrared temperature sensor module
buildNotes: Run the I2C bus at 100 kHz or slower: the MLX90614 SMBus works only between 10 and 100 kHz.
Read a temperature with an SMBus read word: write the RAM address (0x07 object, 0x06 ambient), repeated START, read LSByte then MSByte (the chip then offers a PEC byte).
T = raw × 0.02 − 273.15 °C; if bit 15 of the word is set the reading is an error.
Do not poll it continuously: SCL activity couples into the sensor and skews the reading. Read about once per second.
Point the sensor's window at the object; the field of view of the BAA version is about 90°, so the spot grows with distance.

example.code:
from machine import I2C, Pin
import time
from mlx90614 import MLX90614

i2c = I2C({I2C_ID}, sda=Pin({SDA}), scl=Pin({SCL}), freq=100000)
sensor = MLX90614(i2c)
while True:
    print('Obj=%.1fC Amb=%.1fC' % (sensor.object(), sensor.ambient()))
    time.sleep(1)

test.title: Reports the object and ambient temperatures set on the sliders
